elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence opens "Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement or any Service Option Attachment for any reason, IBM will: ...", so the obligations attach to every covered exit event, not only anticipated expiry.

elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.
elements.evidence: "(a) at Customer's request, provide transition assistance for up to six (6) months" — Vendor-side obligation triggered by Customer request, matching the preferred six-month ceiling.

elements.element: Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.
elements.evidence: "...for up to six (6) months at IBM's then-current rates".

elements.element: Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: "(b) within thirty (30) days, return all Content to Customer"; the thirty-day clock runs from the opening trigger (expiration or termination), not from a request.

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
elements.evidence: "return all Content to Customer in a standard machine-readable format".

elements.element: Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: "(c) after such return, delete all Content from its systems and certify such deletion to Customer in writing" — deletion and written certification are expressly sequenced after return.

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Same inserted trigger language: "Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement or any Service Option Attachment for any reason".

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: The six-month assistance window in limb (a) makes assistance available for a period well in excess of 90 days at Customer's election.

elements.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Limb (b) requires return of all Content within thirty (30) days of the termination/expiration trigger in a machine-readable format.

reasons: The finding is correctly classified as missing: § 3.5 as drafted addresses only acceleration of accrued charges, and neither it nor the survival clause imposes any transition, return, export or deletion obligation.

The single inserted sentence delivers all six preferred elements in operative language (trigger, six-month assistance, then-current rates, 30-day return, machine-readable format, certified deletion after return), so the preferred level is position-complete and the fallback is satisfied a fortiori.

Minimality holds: nothing in the retained § 3.5 payment-acceleration sentence or the survival list was deleted or paraphrased, and the insertion adds no extras (no at-own-expense language, no survival tail, no procedures, no additional remedies) beyond the checklist items.

Extension to "or any Service Option Attachment" is not surplus here because the retained sentence in § 3.5 expressly contemplates termination of selected Service Option Attachments while others continue; without it the exit obligation would not reach a partial termination the contract already structures.

Intent is preserved: the insertion sits in § 3.5, which § 14.2 already lists as surviving, so the obligations remain enforceable post-termination; no cross-reference is broken and the accrued-charges sentence is not contradicted.

One drafting check for the drafter: the insertion relies on "Content" as a defined term. That term is not shown in the resolved definitions supplied here, so confirm the Base Terms define "Content" to include all information, software and data Customer provides; if the definition is narrower than Customer's data as a whole, broaden limb (b)/(c) to "Content and all other Customer data in IBM's possession" to avoid a scope gap and an undefined-term risk.
